source: Dış kaynaklarda saptanan eksik soru tipleri; bağımsız anlatım ve resmî cevap kontrolü (2026-10-13)
answer_convention: İki dilde aynı sırada; ilk şık doğru. Belirsiz cevap aktif bankada yok.
id_convention: Kalıcı idler_030.json; eski veya emekli kimlik yeniden kullanılmaz.

questions.text: For this exercise, the take-off table for the stated mass, pressure altitude and temperature gives a zero-wind paved-runway ground roll of 1,115 ft and a total distance of 2,125 ft to clear a 50 ft obstacle. Its notes require both figures to be reduced by 10% for the 9 kt headwind, then require 15% of the wind-corrected ground roll to be added to the wind-corrected total for dry grass. What total distance is required, rounded to the nearest foot?

A two-leg flight includes a landing at an intermediate aerodrome without refuelling. The cruise times, excluding taxi, take-off and climb, are 45 minutes and 55 minutes. Cruise fuel flow is 6 US gal/h. Each departure requires a separate allowance of 2 US gal for taxi, take-off and climb. The flight plan also specifies a final reserve of 30 minutes at the same cruise fuel flow, to remain after the last landing. With no other allowances required in this exercise, what minimum usable fuel is needed before the first taxi?
The MAC leading edge is 1.50 m aft of datum and MAC length is 1.20 m. Aircraft CG is 1.80 m aft of the same datum. What is CG position in percent MAC?
Under SERA, what is a current flight plan?
options: The flight plan including changes brought about by subsequent clearances
Only the original plan as filed, without subsequent changes
A plan showing only the actual departure time
Any plan filed within the last 24 hours

questions.text: AerodromesA andB are 350 NM apart. From any point on the route, return GS toA is 120 kt and continuing GS toB is 90 kt. Ignore climb, turn time and fuel limits. How far fromA is the point where time toA equals time toB?

Under normal SERA filing periods, a flight will cross international borders or receive air traffic control or advisory service. What minimum predeparture periods apply if it may be subject to ATFM, and for other covered flights? Assume no shorter domestic VFR period is prescribed and no regional exemption applies.
options: 3 h before EOBT for possible ATFM; 60 min beforedeparture for the other flights
60 min before EOBT for possible ATFM; 3 h for the other flights
Only after take-off for both categories

questions.text: For a fictional baggage bay, the permitted floor loading is 300 kg/m² and the compartment gross-load limit is 100 kg. A 5 kg pallet spreads the load over 0.50 m by 0.40 m. CG and access are satisfactory. What maximum baggage mass can be put on the pallet?
A fuel-planning exercise holds engine mass consumption fixed at 24 kg/h. Fuel density changes from 0.80 to 0.75 kg/L. What volumetric consumption corresponds to the same 24 kg/h at the new density?

For this exercise, a VFR flight has planned take-off-to-arrival time 1 h 40 min. At take-off usable fuel is 100 L, including 20 L protected reserve, and constant consumption is 20 L/h. What are Item 19 E/ fuelendurance and Item 16 total EET?

A fictional flight starts with 100 L usable fuel. After 1 h, 70 L remain. The remaining route takes 1 h 40 min and the exercise requires 25 L on arrival. Assuming the observed hourly consumption continues, what arrival fuel and reserve assessment result?
options: 20 L remain, 5 L below the stated reserve
40 L remain, 15 L above the stated reserve
70 L remain, 45 L above the stated reserve
20 L remain, and any positive fuel satisfies the 25 L reserve

questions.text: A private aeroplane uses its full registration TC-ABC as its radiotelephony identity. In ICAO model flight-plan Item 7, how should that registration be entered?
options: ZZZZ because it is a privateflight

questions.text: The SERA standard cruising-level table applies above 3,000 ft AGL, above the transition altitude and below FL 290, with no ATC or competent-authority exception. On a magnetic track of 180°, which listed IFR/VFR pair follows the table?
On the ICAO model paper flight-plan form, how are the listed supplementary equipment categories that are NOT carried indicated in Item 19?
options: Strike out the relevant identifiers for equipment not carried
Circle every identifier for equipment carried
Leave all printed equipment identifiers untouched even when absent
Replace the aircraft identification in Item 7 with those equipment identifiers

questions.text: Zero-fuel mass is 900 kg, MTOM 1,100 kg and maximum landing mass 1,000 kg. Planned trip burn is 50 kg. Tank capacity is 300 kg of usable fuel and all CG limits are satisfied. What maximum take-off fuel mass meets both take-off and landing limits?
A loading sheet defines moment index as moment divided by 1,000. Total moment is 78,500 kg·cm. What index must be entered?

For a return-to-departure planning exercise, usable fuel is 80 L and 20 L must remain on landing. Outbound GS is 100 kt with 15 L/h consumption; return GS 80 kt with 12 L/h. No other allowances are needed. What maximum distance from departure permits an immediate return while keeping the stated reserve?
In a zero-wind cruise exercise, TAS is 120 kt and fuel flow 24 L/h. What is specific air range, the distance travelled through the air per litre?
In a simplified take-off model, acceleration from rest is constant and runway conditions do not change. Required lift-off ground speed increases by 10%. How much does ground-roll distance increase?
On the ICAO model flight-plan form, with the conventional standard-equipment definition and serviceable equipment, what doesS in Item 10 a indicate?
An aircraft type has no assigned ICAO type designator. In the ICAO model flight plan, what entries identify its TYPE?
options: ZZZZ inItem 9 and TYP/ followed by its type inItem 18
NIL inItem 9 and no type information elsewhere

questions.text: During a level take-off roll before lift-off, mass and tyre/runway friction coefficient remain constant. As wing lift increases, what normally happens to wheel normal load and rolling-friction force in the modelF=μ(W−L)?
options: Wheel load decreases but friction must stay constant
Both are independent of wing lift

questions.text: Under SERA, if a flight plan is submitted by radio while airborne, to whom is it transmitted through the available air-ground service?
options: The appropriate air traffic services unit or air-ground control radio station
The search-and-rescue rescue-coordination centre as the routine filing office

questions.text: For runway take-off and landing calculations, where in the standard AIP structure are declared TORA, TODA, ASDA and LDA listed?

Before adding baggage, mass is 800 kg and total moment is 1,600 kg·m. Baggage is loaded at arm 3.00 m. The aft CG limit is 2.10 m and MTOM is 920 kg. All other limits remain satisfied. What maximum baggage mass meets both limits?
In an aeroplane basic-empty-mass record using the modern basic-empty convention, which fuel quantity is normally included?
options: Unusable fuel, with usable fuel excluded
All usable fuel with tanks full

questions.text: For this exercise, an AFM permits Normal-category operation at 700–1,100 kg with CG 1.80–2.20 m, and Utility-category operation at 700–950 kg with CG 1.85–2.05 m. The loaded mass is 1,000 kg and CG 2.00 m. Which category limits are satisfied?
At departure an aeroplane has a mass of 900 kg and a CG 2.00 m aft of datum. It burns 60 kg of fuel whose arm is 2.40 m. No other load changes. Where is the landing CG?
During preflight, what is the most reliable way to establish usable fuel quantity for planning in a light aeroplane?
options: Use the approved visual/dipstick or other POH quantity check and compare with indications and fuel records
Rely solely on the previous pilot saying the tanks are full
Assume the gauge is exact whenever electrical power is on
Use total tank capacity regardless of actual quantity

questions.text: For the stated mass and configuration, a supplied climb table at 4,000 ft gives 450 ft/min at 10°C and 350 ft/min at 30°C. Linear interpolation is authorised. What ROC should be used at 20°C?
A light aeroplane enters a coordinated moderate-bank climbing turn from a straight climb at the same IAS and power. Other conditions are unchanged. What normally happens to ROC?
options: It decreases because additional lift/drag is required for the turn
It remains unchanged because IAS is unchanged
It increases because the bank angle adds vertical lift
It increases whenever the turn is downwind

questions.text: Under SERA, which statement normally applies to a VFR flight across an international border?
options: A flight plan is required unless the States concerned prescribe otherwise
A flight plan is never required if the pilot has a PPL
A flight plan is required only for commercial passenger transport
VMC automatically removes the flight-plan requirement

questions.text: At the stated pressure altitude, a supplied cruise table lists: ISA−20°C/2,300 RPM→105 KTAS,24 L/h; ISA/2,300 RPM→103 KTAS,22 L/h; ISA+20°C/2,300 RPM→101 KTAS,20 L/h. OAT is 20°C below ISA. In zero wind, how much cruise fuel is needed for 210 NM at 2,300 RPM?

A supplied climb table gives cumulative values FROM SEA LEVEL: at 3,000 ft,8 min/2.0 L/9 NM; at 7,000 ft,21 min/5.6 L/24 NM. Under the stated table conditions, what is needed to climb from 3,000 ft to 7,000 ft?

Use these exercise approximations: PA=elevation+(1013−QNH)×30 ft; ISA temperature=15−2×PA(in thousands of feet); DA=PA+120×(OAT−ISA temperature). Elevation is 5,000 ft, QNH 1000 hPa and OAT24.2°C. What is DA?
For steady climb in a propeller aeroplane, which quantity is maximised at the best-rate-of-climb speed Vy?

For this exercise, the POH specifies target approach IAS=normal 65 kt plus HALF the gust increment (gust speed minus mean wind). Wind is 210°/12 kt gusting 22 kt. What target IAS follows this POH instruction?

A landing table gives zero-wind paved ground roll 500 m and total distance over 50 ft 1,200 m. Notes say: reduce both values 10% for 9 kt headwind; then add 45% of the corrected GROUND ROLL for dry grass. What total distance is required with 9 kt headwind on dry grass?

A VFR chart legend explains that its maximum elevation figure (MEF) includes the highest known terrain or obstacle elevation in a grid area, charting allowance and rounding. What does that figure provide?
options: Elevation information for the area; it is not by itself a recommended clearance altitude
The upper limit of controlled airspace

questions.text: In a power-off glide in still air, how does minimum-sink speed normally compare with best-glide speed for maximum distance?
options: It is lower and maximises time aloft rather than distance
It is higher and gives the longest distance
It is identical because both minimise the same quantity

questions.text: For a fictional airfield, the published LDA is 900 m. A currently valid NOTAM states that the last 300 m of that landing direction is closed and revised LDA is 600 m. Required landing distance under actual conditions is 650 m. May this runway be planned for that landing?
options: No, because 650 m exceeds the revised 600 m LDA
Yes, because 650 m is less than the original 900 m
Yes, if the closed portion is used only for braking
Yes, if the pilot rounds 650 m down to 600 m

questions.text: An aeroplane has MTOM 1,050 kg. Its mass including occupants and baggage but excluding usable fuel is 942 kg. CG is within limits throughout, and tank capacity is not limiting. With fuel density 0.72 kg/L, what maximum usable fuel volume can be loaded for take-off?

Actual ramp mass is 1,008 kg, maximum ramp mass 1,010 kg and MTOM 1,000 kg. Fuel density is 0.80 kg/L. No other mass is removed. What minimum fuel consumption before take-off brings mass down to MTOM?
options: No fuel needs to be consumed because ramp mass is within limit

questions.text: An aeroplane enters significant turbulence in cruise. Which speed should the pilot use to reduce structural loads?
options: The AFM/POH turbulence-penetration speed for the actual conditions
VNE because it is the highest permitted speed
A single published VA value regardless of actual mass or POH guidance

questions.text: For the stated mass and temperature, the supplied take-off table gives total distance 1,400 m at 2,000 ft PA and 1,700 m at 4,000 ft PA. The POH permits linear interpolation and no other correction is needed. What total distance applies at 3,000 ft PA?

For this landing exercise, the table gives a zero-wind total distance of 800 m. Its note increases this value by 10% per 2 kt tailwind, up to a 10 kt permitted tailwind. With 6 kt tailwind on the same runway, what total landing distance is required?

Under the stated POH table conditions, zero-wind take-off ground roll is 900 m. The table authorises a tailwind up to 10 kt and specifies an increase of 10% of the zero-wind value for EACH 2 kt tailwind. On the same paved runway with 4 kt tailwind, what ground roll is required?
For a typical normally aspirated piston aeroplane at constant mass and configuration, what happens to the best-rate-of-climb speed expressed as IAS as altitude increases toward the absolute ceiling?
options: It must remain constant because mass is unchanged
It increases at exactly 2% per 1,000 ft for every aeroplane

questions.text: Where should a pilot find the aircraft-specific empty mass, empty CG and loading data needed for preflight mass-and-balance calculations?
options: The current aircraft weight-and-balance records and AFM/POH weight-and-balance/loading section
The normal-procedures checklist without aircraft loading records

questions.text: How are an individual aeroplane initial empty mass and empty CG established for its weight-and-balance record?
options: By weighing that aeroplane in the prescribed condition and calculating its CG from the measured loads
By using one generic mass andCG for every aircraft of the same type
By dividing MTOM by the number of seats
By using the last flight fuel-gauge indication

questions.text: On an ICAO model flight plan where composite Y/Z rules are used, a properly authorised flight begins under VFR and later changes to IFR. Which flight-rules letter belongs inItem 8?
